In [[graph theory]] and [[computer science]], the '''graph sandwich problem''' is a problem of finding a graph that belongs to a particular family of graphs and is "sandwiched" between two other graphs, one of which must be a subgraph and the other of which must be a supergraph of the desired graph.

Graph sandwich problems generalize the problem of testing whether a given graph belongs to a family of graphs, and have attracted attention because of their
applications and as a natural generalization of recognition problems.<ref>{{citation|last1=Golumbic|first1=Martin Charles|last2=Trenk|first2=Ann N.|author2-link= Ann Trenk
 |title=Tolerance Graphs|publisher=Cambridge|year=2004|contribution=Chapter 4. Interval probe graphs and sandwich problems|pages=63–83}}.</ref>

==Problem statement==
More precisely, given a vertex set ''V'', a mandatory edge set ''E''<sup>1</sup>, 
and a (potentially) larger edge set ''E''<sup>2</sup>, 
a graph ''G''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''V'',&nbsp;''E'') is called a ''sandwich'' graph for the pair 
''G''<sup>1</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''V'',&nbsp;''E''<sup>1</sup>), ''G''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''V'',&nbsp;''E''<sup>2</sup>) if 
''E''<sup>1</sup> ⊆ ''E'' ⊆ ''E''<sup>2</sup>.
The ''graph sandwich problem'' for property Π is defined as follows:<ref name="gks">{{citation
 | last1=Golumbic|first1=Martin Charles
 | last2 = Kaplan | first2 = Haim  | last3 = Shamir | first3 = Ron
 | journal = J. Algorithms
 | pages = 449–473
 | title = Graph sandwich problems
 | volume = 19
 | year = 1995 |issue=3
 | doi=10.1006/jagm.1995.1047}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|first=Martin Charles|last=Golumbic|authorlink=Martin Charles Golumbic|title=Algorithmic Graph Theory and Perfect Graphs|edition=2nd|year=2004|series=Annals of Discrete Mathematics|volume=57|publisher=Elsevier|page=279|isbn=978-0-08-052696-6 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8xo-VrWo5_QC&pg=PA279}}.</ref>

:'''Graph Sandwich Problem''' for Property '''Π''':

:'''Instance:''' Vertex set ''V'' and edge sets ''E''<sup>1</sup> ⊆ ''E''<sup>2</sup> ⊆ ''V'' × ''V''.

:'''Question:''' Is there a graph ''G'' = (''V'', ''E'')  such that ''E''<sup>1</sup> ⊆ ''E'' ⊆ ''E''<sup>2</sup> and ''G'' satisfies property Π ?

The ''recognition problem'' for a class of graphs (those satisfying a property Π)
is equivalent to the particular graph sandwich problem where 
''E''<sup>1</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''E''<sup>2</sup>, that is, the optional edge set is empty. 

==Computational complexity==
The graph sandwich problem is [[NP-complete]] when Π is the property of being a [[chordal graph]], [[comparability graph]], [[permutation graph]], [[chordal bipartite graph]], or [[chain graph]].<ref name="gks"/><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = de Figueiredo | first1 = C. M. H.
 | last2 = Faria | first2 = L.
 | last3 = Klein | first3 = S.
 | last4 = Sritharan | first4 = R.
 | doi = 10.1016/j.tcs.2007.04.007
 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = [[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|Theoretical Computer Science]]
 | mr = 2347393
 | pages = 57–67
 | title = On the complexity of the sandwich problems for strongly chordal graphs and chordal bipartite graphs
 | volume = 381
 | year = 2007| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> It can be solved in polynomial time for [[split graph]]s,<ref name="gks"/><ref name="mp">{{citation|last1=Mahadev|first1=N.V.R.|last2=Peled|first2=Uri N.|title=Threshold Graphs and Related Topics|series=Annals of Discrete Mathematics|volume=57|publisher=North-Holland|year=1995|pages=19–22|isbn=978-0-08-054300-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nWfGo_VX5M8C&pg=PA19}}.</ref> [[threshold graph]]s,<ref name="gks"/><ref name="mp"/> and graphs in which every five vertices contain at most one four-vertex [[induced path]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Dantas | first1 = S.
 | last2 = Klein | first2 = S.
 | last3 = Mello| first3 = C.P.
 | last4 = Morgana| first4 = A.
 | doi = 10.1016/j.disc.2008.01.014
 | journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]
 | pages = 3664–3673
 | title = The graph sandwich problem for ''P''<sub>4</sub>-sparse graphs
 | volume = 309
 | year = 2009| issue = 11
 | doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>
The complexity status has also been settled for the ''H''-free graph sandwich problems
for each of the four-vertex graphs ''H''.<ref>{{citation
 | last1=Dantas|first1=Simone 
 | last2 = de Figueiredo| first2 = Celina M.H. 
 | last3 = Maffray| first3 = Frédéric 
 | last4 = Teixeira| first4 = Rafael B.
 | journal = Discrete Applied Mathematics
 | pages = 15–24
 | title = The complexity of forbidden subgraph sandwich problems and the skew partition sandwich problem
 | volume =  182
 | year = 2013 | doi=10.1016/j.dam.2013.09.004| doi-access = free}}.</ref>
